reasons: Comparison section: below sm it is a ul with one li per capability, each holding a p and a dl whose dt/dd pairs carry the three approaches. From sm up it is a table with an sr-only caption, th scope=col for every column header and th scope=row for every capability. The TableScroll wrapper has role=region, an aria-label and tabIndex=0, and the 1440 focus run lists it as a stop.
Included and not-included marks are an aria-hidden SVG plus sr-only text, so meaning does not rest on colour or glyph.

Heading order: h1, then h2 per section, then h3 for beats, plans, 'Included in every plan', problem items and steps. No skipped levels. Feature lists, the two-column 'Included in every plan' list and the ruled lists are real ul/li elements.

Contrast, computed from the tokens in src/cqc_lem/ui/src/index.css: every text pair clears 4.5:1 in both themes (for example light muted #5b6670 on #ffffff about 5.9:1; dark muted #a3aeb8 on #111a22 about 7.5:1). Calculated from hex values, not measured on pixels.
Focus: 30 stops with a visible change and none without one; the order follows the DOM. The global :focus-visible rule uses a 2px currentColor outline. CTA aria-labels begin with the visible text.
Tap targets at 390: buttons and sheet links carry min-h-11 (44px); footer links pass the WCAG 2.5.8 spacing exception.
No horizontal overflow at 1440, 768 or 390 in either theme; the only clipped text is intentional sr-only content. No console errors or failed requests.
Reduced motion is honoured globally, and scrollToSection checks the media query.
The hero screenshot has descriptive alt text inside a figure with a visible figcaption, plus width and height attributes.
NOT VERIFIED: the downscaled full-page phone capture; findings come from the source, the JSON captures and the phone fold.
residuals: The hero screenshot's inner text is image-only; the alt text and caption cover its purpose.
Confirm the phone comparison dt/dd announcement with VoiceOver on iOS.
The sr-only table caption and the region aria-label say nearly the same thing.
No axe or Lighthouse run and no real screen-reader pass; recommended follow-up, not a blocker.
